acceptance: Linux N=3 medians for SF 1 and SF 10 are recorded in the item context and the ADR writer paragraph.
SF 1 peak RSS is at or below 480 MiB in all three runs on both hosts, or the owner accepts the measured margin in writing.
Output SHA-256 for all 8 TPC-H tables is unchanged from the writer-v2 goldens.
description:
## Problem
The ADR performance gate requires measurements on the Linux runner for PRs touching the streaming converter; #4539 and #4552 were measured only on a loaded macOS host. After #4552 the TPC-H medians are SF 1 4.23 s / 497.0 MiB (runs 489.5, 497.0, 510.6 against 512 MiB) and SF 10 46.0 s / 640.5 MiB; unmodified develop before it measured a 519.0 MiB median, over budget. The reader queue depth was cut from 32 to 4 to hold memory, costing about 1 s at SF 1 and 14 s at SF 10.

## Change
Run the converter gate (TPC-H, 10-chunk zstd input, N=3) on the Linux CI/agent runner and record it; find where the combine-to-row-group step holds memory and regain headroom without raising wall time; decide whether the gate becomes a scheduled CI measurement.

## Decision gates
- If Linux medians miss the budget, report to the owner with the profile before changing the budget or the code path.
- No change may alter Parquet bytes without a writer-identity bump.

## Guardrails
- BenchBox work only in a linked worktree (make worktree-create, make agent-write-preflight); the primary clone is read-only.
- Heavy work only through make heavy-run; never bypass or signal the lock, and never kill processes by name pattern (pkill -f); stop only PIDs you started.
- Commits as the configured human identity; no agent attribution.
- No carried or own reimplementation of upstream code without the owner decision recorded in datagen-decision-upstream-gap-policy.
- A choice between a small and a large implementation path goes to the owner with sizes before work starts.
- Report only results that were observed; name anything not run.
